source.title: Fundamental Structure (I. Static Aspect, II. Dynamic Aspect)
source.author: Ñāṇavīra Thera

source_span.quote: two things define a thing, namely the difference between them

claims.claim_text: A thing is defined by the difference between two things; identity is structurally dependent on contrast rather than a hidden substrate.
claims.hetu: difference is required to distinguish two things
claims.sadhya: identity is structurally determined by contrast
claims.vyapti_statement: If a thing is identifiable only through difference from another thing, then identity is contrast-structured rather than substance-grounded.

falsifier.condition: Give a coherent account in which a thing is determinate without contrast, priority, exclusion, relation, or any equivalent differentiating condition.

claims.reasoning: This is Nanavira's base structural claim. It directly supports the no-hidden-substance side of the reflexivity dossier while remaining narrower than a full Buddhist apoha theory.

source_span.quote: the difference between them, clearly, is what has to be done to pass from one to the other, or the operation of transforming one into the other

claims.claim_text: Difference is an operation of transformation or interchange between terms, not a static property merely attached to one term.
claims.hetu: difference is what must be done to pass from one term to another
claims.vyapti_statement: If difference is the passage or interchange between terms, then difference should be modeled as a relation/operation rather than an intrinsic isolated property.

falsifier.condition: Show that Nanavira's transformation reading is eliminable while preserving his distinction between one thing and two things.

claims.reasoning: This gives the structural-reflexivity candidate a dynamic operator: relation is not a label but a transform between terms.

source_span.quote: Duration and Invariance under Transformation are one and the same.

claims.claim_text: Duration is equivalent to invariance under transformation: endurance is the persistence of structure across change.
claims.sadhya: enduring identity is invariance under transformation
claims.vyapti_statement: If endurance requires both unchange and change, then the stable identity of a thing is its invariant structure under transformation.

falsifier.condition: Construct a duration model in which something endures through change without any invariant structure or equivalent persistence condition.

claims.reasoning: This is the strongest bridge from Nanavira's static analysis to a dynamic account of identity and recognition.

source_span.quote: the structure of first-order reflexion has the same structure as the immediate thing

claims.claim_text: Reflexion is self-similar across levels: the structure of structure has the structure of structure.
claims.hetu: higher-order reflexion repeats the same structural form as immediate presentation
claims.sadhya: reflexivity can be modeled structurally without adding a second substance
claims.vyapti_statement: If reflexion repeats the form of immediate structure at a higher level, then reflexivity need not require a different entity or hidden owner.

falsifier.condition: Show that reflexion necessarily changes its object in kind, so that higher-order structure cannot preserve the form of immediate experience.

claims.reasoning: This is the direct Nanavira support for structural reflexivity in the dossier. It supports the candidate without proving or denying intrinsic manifestness.

source_span.quote: Past and future exist in the present as past and as future.

claims.claim_text: Past and future are present as structured determinations, not as independent temporal regions outside the present.
claims.hetu: the general/particular hierarchy is interchangeable with the past/present/future hierarchy
claims.sadhya: temporal structure is internally present as differentiated determination
claims.vyapti_statement: If temporal relations are generated by hierarchy, then past and future can be present as past and future without existing as external regions.
vyapti_violations: The local source text gives a compressed summary; full McTaggart reconstruction is needed before this can strongly affect the reflexivity question.

falsifier.condition: Show that the hierarchy cannot resolve A-series/B-series tension without equivocation between temporal and logical priority.

claims.reasoning: Relevant as background to structural invariance and reflexion, but weaker for the core reflexivity crux.

source_span.quote: If a thing endures, it endures for ever. A thing is eternal.

claims.claim_text: A thing is eternal only relative to its level of analysis; the hierarchy leaves no place for anything absolutely enduring or absolutely durationless.
claims.hetu: absolute difference between changing and unchanging is required for duration at a level
claims.sadhya: eternity is level-relative rather than absolute substancehood
claims.vyapti_statement: If endurance is defined within hierarchical levels, then eternity should be scoped to level rather than treated as an absolute metaphysical substance.

falsifier.condition: Show that Nanavira's hierarchy entails an absolutely enduring entity rather than only level-relative invariance.

claims.reasoning: This pressures the move from local reflexivity to universal substance. It does not attack intrinsic manifestness directly.

source_span.quote: two things define a thing, namely the difference between them

claims.claim_text: Nanavira's difference-based determination is a bridge candidate to Dharmakirti's apoha, but not yet the same formal node.
claims.hetu: both accounts use difference/exclusion to explain determination without substance
claims.sadhya: Nanavira difference and Dharmakirti apoha overlap structurally
claims.vyapti_statement: If two independently scoped accounts use difference/exclusion to explain determination without substance, then they may share a formal bridge node.
vyapti_violations: Nanavira is presenting a phenomenological/combinatorial structure, while Dharmakirti's apoha is a semantic and epistemological theory.
Apoha concerns exclusion in concept/meaning; Nanavira's base claim concerns ontological or experiential determination.

falsifier.condition: Run relation probing after both claims are formalized; if neither SUBSUMES nor BRIDGES is found, keep them as OVERLAPS rather than merged nodes.

claims.reasoning: This is deliberately weak and bridge-seeking. It should never collapse the two traditions without formal or reviewed relation evidence.
